source.check: 'Mr. William M'Dowell was elected as representative for Ardkeen. He gained a majority of 61 over his opponent Mr. T. N. M'Lay' (page image read); the nominations report gives the straight fight between Mr. W. M'Dowell and Mr. N. M'Lay, both of Cloughey

note: Triennial election of North Down (Newtownards) Rural District Council, 1955 (Co. Down county and rural poll day Thursday 2 June 1955). Nominations closed on Tuesday 17 May: only Ardkeen was contested; fourteen retiring members were returned unopposed (the report does not name them); and three divisions had no nomination, where the retiring members for Kilmood and Newtownards North were deemed re-elected and Crawfordsburn, whose member Mr. W. Henderson had died, stayed vacant until the next election (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8; Northern Whig, 18 May 1955, p. 5). Mr. William McCutcheon was co-opted to the council at its annual meeting in June 1955, not as Crawfordsburn's member (North Down Herald, 18 June 1955, p. 6). Polled. Only the majority (61) is printed; the vote figures are not given in the reports read, so none are recorded. M'Dowell succeeded the retiring member, Mrs. H. T. Kelly.
